title: CatalogPipeline v1
description: The contract every publish pipeline file is held to. A provider adding a capability writes a file declaring `schemaRef: {uses: publish.oan/CatalogPipeline/v1}` and is checked against this every time a run loads it: a file that does not match is REFUSED, naming the path that is wrong (and is never kept as the last good copy), rather than failing at 00:00 against a live upstream or silently declaring a rule nothing enforces. additionalProperties is false everywhere on purpose -- a misspelled key is the failure this exists to catch. Every `description` below states the failure its rule prevents, so this file is also the documentation; MandiPrice/publish/agmarknet.yaml is a complete working example.

then.description: An upstream's address comes from inputs.baseUrl.
A token exchange posts inputs.tokenUser and inputs.tokenSecret.
An HTTP step calls the upstream; a file with one and no upstream block has nowhere to call.

apiVersion.description: Kubernetes-style identity, kept for familiarity. It must AGREE with schemaRef.uses; the engine refuses a file where the two disagree rather than picking one silently.

pipeline.description: The steps, in order. An empty pipeline produces an empty collection and a run that reads as 'this provider has nothing', so at least one step is required.

schemaRef.description: Which contract this file was written against. A map rather than a bare string so it can gain keys later without every provider's file having to change shape.

uses.description: The contract id. The engine resolves it to a schema it embeds; an id it does not carry is refused, naming the ones it does.

name.description: Names the catalog files on disk. Three things must agree on it: what writes them, what sweeps the previous run's, and the glob the publish step sends from.

capability.description: The registry's capability code, e.g. openagrinet:MandiPrice. This is the run's identity: the run log and the output directory are keyed on it, and the engine refuses if the collector claims a different one.

cron.description: Standard FIVE-field cron: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. The six-field seconds variant is refused, because the two are indistinguishable by shape and a pasted six-field expression would run hourly while looking daily.

utcOffset.description: A fixed offset from UTC, e.g. +05:30, or Z for UTC itself. The cron is resolved HERE, not on the host's clock: a UTC host reading a midnight-IST schedule off its own clock fires on the wrong calendar day and asks the upstream for yesterday. A fixed offset rather than an IANA zone name, because this engine never needs a zoneinfo database: every network it serves has one offset, year round, with no daylight saving to track.

inputs.description: The flag/env surface, resolved flag > env > default. A pipeline with an upstream must declare baseUrl, and one whose upstream exchanges a token must also declare tokenUser and tokenSecret (see the root allOf): the engine reads them by name, so a file spelling them differently fails at load instead of at the token exchange. A pipeline with no upstream needs none of them.

type.description: Anything else is refused rather than passed through: passing an unrecognised type through verbatim is how the literal word 'today' once reached an upstream as a date.

format.description: For type: date -- the layout the UPSTREAM reads, e.g. dd-MM-yyyy. Not ISO unless the upstream says so.

secret.description: Marks a credential. A secret input is redacted wherever inputs are printed; it never appears in a log line or an error.

required.description: Refuse the run when this input resolves to empty, naming it and its env. For values with no safe default, such as the identity a catalog publishes under.

errors.description: How this upstream's failures are classified. Classification, not cosmetics: recording 'no rows' as a failure once turned 27 of 36 quiet regions into 27 reported outages.

allowCleartext.description: Permits an http:// upstream that is not loopback. Off by default, because the credential exchange and every token after it travel over this address. It exists because some upstreams offer no TLS at all, and a rule that makes a real integration impossible gets worked around rather than obeyed. Setting it is a deliberate decision recorded in this file and warned about on every run -- not an accident of an unset variable.

kind.description: tokenExchange (the default when kind is omitted) posts credentials and receives a token. none is for an upstream that needs no credential. apiKey carries an input's value, placed per token.carriedAs and token.name, with no round trip.

then.description: A tokenExchange (including an auth block with no kind) with no request has no endpoint to call, and with no token.at has nowhere to read the token from.
An apiKey needs the input holding the key and where it rides.

path.description: The token endpoint, relative to upstream.baseUrl. Declared here rather than in Go so a second provider authenticates without an engine change.

body.description: The JSON the token endpoint expects. Values are ${inputs.*} references -- the credentials themselves are never in this file, only the NAME of the input that holds them.

at.description: Where the token sits in the response, as a path from the root: $.token, $.data.access_token. A path rather than an expression on purpose -- this runs on a response carrying a live credential, and a path cannot do anything but select.

carriedAs.description: How the credential rides on later requests. header: on every request. query: on POST the client adds it; on GET the step's mapping places it, so it is never sent twice.

reexchangeOn.description: Statuses that mean the token died, e.g. [401, 403]. Re-exchanged on these rather than refreshed on a timer, because this class of upstream returns no expiry.

value.description: apiKey only: the input holding the key, as ${inputs.name}. Never the key itself.

errorRule.description: A rule either MATCHES on when, or is the default catch-all. Never both -- a rule that is both is ambiguous about which branch applies.

classify.description: emptyResult means the upstream answered 'nothing here' -- a coverage fact to count and continue past. transportError is an outage. reauth means the token died and is re-exchanged (see auth.token.reexchangeOn). Collapsing emptyResult into transportError is the mistake that once turned 27 of 36 quiet regions into 27 reported outages. NOTE: a step's onError today dispatches on emptyResult and transportError only; reauth is handled by the client, not by a step.

id.description: Names this step in logs and errors. A run is minutes long and mostly silent; this is what tells 'stuck on step 3' from 'merely slow'.

uses.description: The primitive. A name the engine does not implement is REFUSED rather than skipped -- a step that silently does nothing is a rule the file states and nothing performs.

out.description: Names this step's output so later steps and the catalog block can reference it as ${name}.

when.description: A JSONata predicate. ${...} inside it is substituted as a LITERAL, not raw text: raw substitution turns ${inputs.mode} = 'skip' into a comparison against a record field that does not exist, so the rule silently never fires.

else.description: What this step yields when `when` is false.

failWhenEmpty.description: A refusal, not a warning, carrying the message an operator reads. An empty collection walks cleanly through every later step and produces a well-formed, zero-error, empty run.

forEach.description: A ${...} reference to the collection to loop over.

as.description: Names the loop variable, reachable as ${name.field}.

concurrency.description: Only 1 is honoured, and anything higher is REFUSED rather than silently ignored. The JSONata evaluator this shares is not safe to run in parallel, and a file stating a parallelism that never happens is a lie the reader cannot see.

onError.description: Keyed by classification (emptyResult, transportError, reauth). A failure with no matching entry ABORTS -- a swallowed error is worse than a loud one.

then.description: A loop with no `as` has no name for its variable, so nothing inside it can reference the item.
An HTTP step needs somewhere to call and a mapping to shape the call with.
A const step with no records would produce an empty collection and a run that reads as 'nothing to publish'.

record.description: The counter this outcome is recorded in. The file names it; the engine only counts.

continue.description: Whether the loop carries on. This is what keeps one region's empty answer from ending a thirty-six region collection.

with.description: A step's parameters. The union of what every primitive takes, because steps are heterogeneous; which keys are required depends on `uses` (see the conditionals on step).

mapping.description: Relative to the mappings/ directory beside the pipeline file.

local.description: Values handed to the mapping, typically including ${auth.token}. The mapping decides where each one lands in the request.

on.description: The key both sides are matched on.

type.description: Only a left join is implemented. A left row with no match is KEPT: it is a real record whose extra fields are merely unknown.

carry.description: Fields carried across from the right side.

rules.description: Ordered; the FIRST match wins, so a file reads top to bottom. A rule with no `when` is the default and must come last -- a record matching no rule is an error, not an unset field.

then.description: Follow-up edits. `clear` removes fields, which is how a value that cannot be believed is prevented from being published as though it could.

key.description: The key a dedupe collapses on; the first occurrence is kept.

records.description: A const step's output, written in the file. How a pipeline with no upstream -- a catalog whose content is fixed -- still hands the catalog block a collection.

of.description: A concat step's inputs: ${...} references to collections, appended in the order listed.

groupBy.description: The field records are grouped by -- one catalog per group. A group left with nothing publishable produces NO catalog rather than an empty one: publishing an empty catalog retires that group's resources from the network on the next MERGE.

reason.description: Stated, not implied: an excluded record is counted under this reason so somebody can find out which and why.

as.description: The boolean field set on matching records. They stay in the catalog.

order.description: Makes a run read the same way twice, and fixes which records land in which chunk.

by.description: The order a group is SPLIT in: it decides which records land in which chunk. Use a key new records sort to the end of (an id), so adding a record never moves others between catalogIds -- under MERGE the old copy would never be removed.

renderBy.description: Optional. The order a reader sees inside each catalog, applied after the split: keys in turn, text case-insensitively, numbers numerically.

catalogId.description: The network-facing id template, e.g. catalog:example:${slug}. A catalog with no id cannot be published.

mapping.description: The JSONata mapping that turns a chunk into a catalog document. Use this, or mappingByField with mappings, not both.

mappingByField.description: The record field that says which kind of catalog a chunk is (for example kind). A chunk's kind is its first record's value; a group is always one kind.

mappings.description: For each value of mappingByField, the JSONata mapping that renders a chunk of that kind. A kind with no entry is an error.

chunk.description: Splits a group so no catalog exceeds what the far end will index.

budget.description: The cap per catalog. For Discovery this is 256 geometries, counted CUMULATIVELY per catalogId -- a catalog over it indexes PARTIAL, meaning it goes in with resources missing and nothing downstream says so.

cost.description: What one record costs against the budget, as JSONata. It MUST agree with what the render actually emits -- if it counts records the render does not emit as geometries, a catalog silently goes over the cap.

slug.description: Names each chunk, e.g. ${group}${chunkIndex > 1 ? '-' & chunkIndex : ''}. Chunk 1 keeps the bare group name so a group that stops splitting does not orphan its first catalog.

refuseSplitWhen.description: JSONata over a group's first publishable record. When true and the group would need more than one chunk, the run fails instead of splitting. For groups whose membership must not move between catalogIds: under MERGE a moved resource leaves a stale copy in its old catalog.

refuseWhen.description: The one refusal form understood: collection.<counter> > <N>, where <counter> is a name this file's own steps record into and N the number of failures tolerated (0 refuses on any). A partial collection must never publish as though it were whole.

retireOld.description: Deactivates a superseded catalog: an isActive:false catalog with no resources, built by the Publisher with the same envelope builder as every publish, carrying this deployment's identity. Typically a ONE-TIME migration, so `enabled` points at an input that defaults to false.

enabled.description: A ${inputs.*} reference. The publish step REFUSES an enable flag it cannot resolve: reading an unresolvable flag as 'off' would silently skip a retirement an operator asked for.

isActive.description: A retirement deactivates; only false is meaningful, and true is refused.

updateMode.description: MERGE (default) or FULL, passed to the directive as written. Note: /publish currently rejects FULL.

catalogType.description: The directive's catalogType; REGULAR when omitted.

visibleTo.description: The networks the retirement is visible to -- match the catalogs that supersede it, e.g. [${inputs.networkId}]. Entries may be ${inputs.*} references.

schemaTypes.description: The retired catalog's JSON-LD schema contexts, sent as the directive's schemaTypes and context.schemaContext. Entries may be ${inputs.*} references.
